    Corporate Gift-Giving Etiquette in Vietnam: What to Give, When and How

    October 22, 2026|Huynh Nguyen

    Corporate gift giving etiquette in Vietnam comes down to three choices: give at the right moment, with Tet as the most important occasion of the year; choose something useful and well made rather than cash; and present it with care, usually at the end of a meeting. Get those right and the gift does its quiet work, which is to say thank you and signal that the relationship matters.

    For managers who have recently arrived in Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi, the customs can feel unwritten. They are, but they are also consistent. Here is what to know.

    When do companies in Vietnam give gifts?

    Tet, the Lunar New Year, is the most important corporate gift-giving occasion in Vietnam (AHK Vietnam). In the weeks before the holiday, companies send gifts to clients, partners and suppliers, and many teams plan their Tet corporate gift in Vietnam well ahead, because the holiday closes much of the country for several days.

    Beyond Tet, gifts commonly appear at a few other moments:

    • Year-end client appreciation, often tied to a customer conference or dinner.
    • A first meeting or a visit to a partner's office, where a modest gift opens the relationship.
    • Milestones, such as a signed agreement, an office opening or a long partnership.

    The occasion shapes the gift. A Tet gift carries wishes for the year ahead; a client appreciation gift says thank you for the year that has passed.

    What makes a good corporate gift in Vietnam?

    Typical business gifts include branded pens, good coffee or tea, and desk accessories (Vietnam Tourism). What these have in common is useful, modest and easy to accept.

    A good gift for a Vietnamese partner tends to be:

    • Useful in daily work, so it is seen and remembered.
    • Well made, because quality reflects on the giver.
    • Appropriate in value, generous enough to show respect but never so expensive that it creates obligation.
    • Thoughtfully presented, since wrapping and packaging are part of the message.

    What does corporate gift giving etiquette in Vietnam say to avoid?

    Some mistakes are easy to make if you have not been told. The guidance below is drawn from Vietnam Tourism.

    Do Avoid
    Give at the end of the meeting Giving cash in a business context, which can read as a bribe
    Choose red, gold or yellow wrapping Black wrapping, which is associated with funerals; white is also linked with mourning
    Give practical items: desk pieces, coffee, tea, pens Knives, scissors or other sharp objects, which suggest cutting the relationship
    Present the gift with both hands Handkerchiefs, clocks and watches, and sets of four

    How should you present a corporate gift?

    The handover matters as much as the object.

    1. Wait until the end of the meeting. Gifts are usually given as the meeting closes, not at the start.
    2. Use both hands. Present the gift with both hands; the recipient will usually receive it the same way.
    3. Do not expect it to be opened. The recipient will likely set it aside to open later. This is courtesy, not indifference, so do not insist.

    Why do lasting gifts tend to be appreciated?

    Consumables are pleasant and gone within a week. An object used every day keeps the relationship present long after the season. For a client appreciation leather gift, the most useful pieces are the ones that fit a working life:

    • A leather passport holder for partners who travel often. It is personal without being intimate, and goes on every trip.
    • A leather luggage tag, a small gift that suits a larger team or pairs with a passport holder, as in our passport holder and luggage tag set.
    • A desk tray, such as the Square Leather Valet Tray with Corner Snap, which holds keys, wallet and phone and keeps its shape thanks to four riveted corners.
    • A desk set, like the Office Desk Set, which can be personalized by debossing, silver foil or gold foil.

    Leather also changes with use. It softens and develops a patina, so the gift becomes more personal over time. A logo can be added by blind debossing for a discreet finish, or by foil stamping where you want it to show.     FAQ

    When is the main corporate gift season in Vietnam?
    Tet, the Lunar New Year, is the most important occasion. Companies typically send gifts to clients and partners in the weeks before the holiday.

    Is it acceptable to give cash to a business partner in Vietnam?
    No. Cash in a business context can be read as a bribe. Choose a practical, well-made gift instead.

    How do I hand over a gift at a meeting?
    Wait until the end of the meeting and present it with both hands. Do not expect the recipient to open it in front of you.

    What colors should I avoid when wrapping a gift?
    Avoid black, which is associated with funerals, and white, which is linked with mourning. Red, gold and yellow are safe choices.

    Is a leather passport holder a suitable corporate gift?
    Yes. It is useful, personal without being intimate, and can carry a discreet company logo.
